important_information: Documented tables enumerate ordered operand comparisons for ==, >, <, >= and <= across 18 representative values/types; each row is left operand and each column right operand. All cells read through lossless compact normalization.

Equality with booleans is coercive: True compares equal to positive/negative numbers, nonempty strings, filled arrays and filled vectors; False equals zero, null, empty string/array, zero vector, uninitialized variable, unspawned hero and listed entity values.
Tables document asymmetric equality: empty custom string and zero vector compare equal to Null Entity, but reversing those operands does not; ordinary symmetry assumptions are unsafe.

Tables document non-transitive-looking coercion: False equals Null and Empty Array, while Null does not equal Empty Array. Equality and ordering do not form ordinary cross-type algebra: True equals a positive number yet is less than it in the table.
Non-null Entity is listed as equal to False, Null and zero; entity presence must not be inferred from generic truthiness without verifying entity semantics.
Hero of unspawned player is equal to Empty Array in both directions, but not Null in equality; out-of-bounds First element of Empty Array behaves like null/zero in several equality comparisons.
Article proposes testing nonzero vector by A == True or boolean context; this is a narrowly typed shortcut, not a safe generic value test.

Verification procedure exists: PC-only Inspector log-file option, import C89J3 (editor backup URL present), spawn, wait for completion, extract operation tables from log; reduce comparisons per tick or increase ticks between batches if the harness crashes.

important_information: Documented Inspector recording adds runtime cost, particularly for array modifications; disable after debugging for releases.
Waitless action bursts can exhaust a tick's workload; yield or batch when simultaneous completion is unnecessary, rather than treating all finite loops as equally unsafe.
Rule conditions are documented as ordered and short-circuiting; put cheap/selective gating before expensive array/spatial calculations. Article recommends less frequently changing conditions early.
Player hero/slot filters reduce evaluation scope, but changing away from that hero/slot immediately aborts an active rule; optimization changes lifecycle behavior.

Startup load can be reduced by delaying initialization until spawn, gating expensive conditions, consolidating selected rules, and staggering player initialization with Wait(Slot Of(Event Player)*0.016).

Sparse evaluation moves expensive conditions into an If inside a waited loop; example polls at 0.2 seconds instead of 0.016, trading reaction precision for cost. It can miss timing-sensitive behavior and is not interchangeable with per-tick event checks.

Disabled rules/actions/conditions and empty rules reportedly do not consume execution cost, although empty rules still appear in Inspector. This differs from element counting, where disabling does not reclaim elements.

Mutating any array element reportedly causes every rule condition referencing that variable to be reconsidered, even if they reference a different index; monolithic state arrays can amplify invalidation.

Damage-event rules cannot rerun for the same active context while waiting; a Wait used as throttling can discard needed triggers. Dealt Damage is per attacker, so simultaneous multi-target damage can process only one victim; Took Damage is per victim and allows one active instance for each victim.
High-frequency SMG/DOT/beam damage events can dominate load; any wait-based reduction must explicitly consider which event information will be lost.
Built-in Mapped/Filtered/Sorted Array operations are documented as often cheaper than manual For Global Variable loops; multidimensional array processing is expensive.

An anti-crash fallback lowers slow-motion speed when Server Load crosses a threshold and restores speed below a second threshold; source explains slower tick rate gives more computation time, at the cost of gameplay slowdown. It is a mitigation rather than guaranteed prevention.

Article reports periodic load spikes associated with replay/killcam/POTG snapshots, disappearing after about 1h30 when replay/killcam recording stops; reduce players/bots/text/effects to limit impact.
Practice range is documented at approximately 20.8333 ticks/sec versus normal maps' 62.5; timing/performance validation should occur on target maps.
Article associates variability by time/day/patch activity and missing hero-select entries with server pressure; aim for headroom rather than a barely passing test.
uncertainties: Archived 2025 guidance is not independently measured; many numeric thresholds (20 actions, hundreds of rules, server-load 230/200) are examples, not universal limits.
Batching pseudocode uses Global.batch == 0 for reset and mixes syntax; not copy-ready.
Claims about server traffic and replay-spike cause are anecdotal/speculative ('most likely'); retain that distinction.
A second dynamic slow-motion formula and prose '0-15%' range do not obviously match (defaults at Server Load 150 already reduce speed about 20%); verify before recommending.
Statement that wait placement does not matter concerns workload only; scheduling, side effects and event loss make placement semantically significant.
Blanket 'avoid shared first conditions' and 'healthy mix of events' are heuristics, not validated generally optimal transformations.

Projection places text on a plane from eye position plus right/up/facing components. Custom-camera right axis comes from a cross product; upward basis derives from facing angles with vertical angle minus 90.
Do Not Clip prevents map geometry/viewmodel occlusion. Constants 100,3,0.2 are trial-and-error; distant placement reduces camera sway but can exceed world bounds and require retuning scale/offset.
